subject: Logic
title: Advertising Logic
description: A short lesson to help you apply Advertising Logic.

hook.text: Nine out of ten dentists recommend this toothpaste. That leaves out what the tenth said—and who paid the nine.

buildup.text: Ads use logical shortcuts: authority appeals, emotional triggers, and implied but unproven claims.

discovery.text: Weasel words do heavy lifting: helps reduce, up to 50% off, part of a balanced diet. None promise anything.

twist.text: The most effective ads bypass logic entirely—they associate the product with identity and belonging.

climax.text: Treat every ad like an argument: what's the claim, what's the evidence, and what's being left unsaid?

punchline.text: Ads argue. They just hide the argument.

quiz.question: What are weasel words in advertising?
options: Vague terms that imply claims without promising anything
